name: Arkansas Mountain

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, hot summer

climate: Few classic table-wine grapes keep their freshness in heat like this. It suits fortified wine, table grapes and raisins.

soil.rock: Shale and mudstone are fine-grained rocks that hold heat well and are moderately fertile. Sandstone is sand bound into rock. It weathers to light, sandy soil that drains freely.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. It is very acid, which locks up nutrients, so growers spread lime to raise the pH.

land: The high ground runs about 4°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Best for big crops of everyday wine, or table grapes.
